blocks.text: This chapter introduces data and its analysis in modern computing: the basics of data science; structured and unstructured data and how data is collected and stored; machine learning as a way for systems to learn from data and make decisions; how to evaluate a model with accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score and improve it through validation and tuning; and finally common tools such as Excel, R and Python.

blocks.title: Data science
blocks.text: Data science is the field of collecting, organising, analysing and interpreting data to find useful information and support decision-making.

Data science converts raw data into meaningful knowledge, using tools and methods that can analyse large amounts of data. It supports decisions in many areas, helps predict future trends, and is widely used in business, education and healthcare. It studies data to discover patterns: data is collected from different sources, cleaned and organised, analysed, and the results are interpreted carefully (Fig 6.1). It answers questions with facts and reduces guesswork.

blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: 1 collection (gather and process), 2 exploring (explore and clean), 3 modelling (train and test) and 4 decision making (insights and actions). A dashed purple feedback loop runs from decision making back to collection: results lead to new questions and new data. A note lists the fields data science draws on.
blocks.caption: The data science workflow (original diagram after Fig 6.1).
blocks.long_description: The loop matters: what is learned from one analysis usually raises the next question, so data science is repeated rather than done once.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Many organisations use data science to support decision-making; it helps them see trends and patterns hidden in data.

items: Mathematics: working with numbers and calculations.
Computer science: tools and programming skills.
Domain knowledge: understanding the real problem.

blocks.text: Because it combines these fields, each supporting the others, data science is called interdisciplinary.
